extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political philosophy, law, and governance (readers of Hobbesian theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and evaluative principles from Hobbes' Leviathan chapters on trade, money, colonies, counsel, and civil laws — guidance for constituting sovereign authority, making law, and assessing counsel and public finance. Useful for analyzing or applying Hobbesian criteria for legitimate legislation, counsel, and public institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign regulation of foreign trade
rubrics_metrics.description: It belongeth to the Common-wealth (that is, to the Soveraign only,) to approve, or disapprove both of the places, and matter of forraign Traffique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign alone decides where and for what commodities subjects may traffic abroad; private discretion in such matters is dangerous because individuals might trade to private gain in ways injurious or unprofitable to the commonwealth (e.g., furnish enemies or import noxious goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign authority over transfer of property and contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: It belongeth to the Common-wealth... to appoint in what manner, all kinds of contract between Subjects (as buying, selling, exchanging, borrowing, lending, letting, and taking to hire,) are to bee made; and by what words, and signes they shall be understood for valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form, validity, and language of contracts are specified by the sovereign; procedures for exchange and transfer of nourishment/commodities must be established centrally to sustain the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money defined as the 'concoction' or circulating nourishment of the commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: By Concoction, I understand the reducing of all commodities... to some thing of equal value, and withall so portably, as not to hinder the motion of men from place to place... And this is nothing else but Gold, and Silver, and Mony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Money should convert stored commodities into a portable, equivalent measure so individuals can carry nourishment/value across places; money is analogized to blood circulating to nourish the body politic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of stable, effective money
rubrics_metrics.description: Gold and Silver... is a commodious measure for the value of all things else between Nations; and Mony... is a sufficient measure of the value of all things else, between the Subjects of that Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective money is widely valued across nations (portable internationally), derives value from its matter (intrinsic/precious metal), and thus resists arbitrary alteration by a single state; such money enables national projection (armies, travellers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instability of base/local coin
rubrics_metrics.description: But that Coyne, which is not considerable for the Matter, but for the Stamp of the place... hath its effect at home only; where also it is subject to the change of Laws, and thereby to have the value diminished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coins whose value depends on stamp or legal status (not intrinsic matter) are vulnerable to local legal change and loss of value; they cannot serve reliably across borders or in times of change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public finance requires defined conduits and offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conduits, and Wayes by which it is conveyed to the Publique use, are of two sorts; One, that Conveyeth it to the Publique Coffers; The Other, that Issueth the same out againe for publique payments. Of the first sort, are Collectors, Receivers, and Treasurers; of the second are the Treasurers againe, and the Officers appointed for payment...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A functioning commonwealth needs clear institutional roles for collecting public revenue and disbursing payments; the analogy to veins/heart stresses orderly circulation and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonies derive rights from sovereign authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Right of Colonies (saving Honour, and League with their Metropolis,) dependeth wholly on their Licence, or Letters, by which their Soveraign authorised them to Plant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a colony is autonomous (a new commonwealth) or a province depends on the license/letters granted by the founding sovereign; the metropolis may renounce control (emancipate) or retain provincial status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command versus Counsel — definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: COMMAND is, where a man saith, 'Doe this,' or 'Doe this not,' without expecting other reason than the Will of him that sayes it. COUNSELL, is where a man saith, 'Doe' or 'Doe not this,' and deduceth his own reasons from the benefit that arriveth by it to him to whom he saith it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish imperatives grounded in the will/interest of the commander (binding) from advice aimed at another's benefit (non-binding); confusion of the terms causes mistakes in interpreting texts and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding force and obligations of command vs counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A man may be obliged to do what he is Commanded; as when he hath covenanted to obey: But he cannot be obliged to do as he is Counselled, because the hurt of not following it, is his own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands create enforceable obligations (especially under covenant); counsel cannot obligate unless transformed into command by prior covenant or promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of counsel given when asked
rubrics_metrics.description: He that giveth counsell to his Soveraign, (whether a Monarch, or an Assembly) when he asketh it, cannot in equity be punished for it, whether the same be conformable to the opinion of the most, or not, so it be to the Proposition in debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person asked for counsel is protected from punishment for the advice given (sovereign is author of asking); by contrast, a subject who counsels another to break law is punishable because ignorance of law is no excuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhortation/dehortation as counsel vehemently pressed
rubrics_metrics.description: EXHORTATION, and DEHORTATION, is Counsell, accompanied with signes in him that giveth it, of vehement desire to have it followed... they have in their speeches, a regard to the common Passions... and make use of Similitudes, Metaphors, Examples, and other tooles of Oratory, to perswade...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhortation employs rhetoric and passions rather than strict reasoning; it is suited to influencing multitudes and may serve private interests (thus can be corrupt when used where calm counsel is required).

rubrics_metrics.name: When exhortation is appropriate and when it becomes command
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a man may lawfully Command, as a Father in his Family, or a Leader in an Army, his Exhortations and Dehortations, are not onely lawfull, but also necessary, and laudable: But then they are no more Counsells, but Commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders who have lawful command may properly use exhortatory language to enforce execution; in those contexts exhortation functions as a softened command rather than pure counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corruption of counsellors who use exhortation for self-interest
rubrics_metrics.description: They that Exhort and Dehort, where they are required to give Counsell, are corrupt Counsellours, and as it were bribed by their own interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When advisers substitute passion and rhetoric aimed at their own benefit for impartial reasoning directed at the advisee's good, their counsel is corrupt and unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: First condition of a good counsellor: aligned ends
rubrics_metrics.description: That His Ends, And Interest, Be Not Inconsistent With The Ends And Interest Of Him He Counselleth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisers must not have ends that conflict with the advisee's interests; otherwise their advice is suspect and likely self-serving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of good counsel: clear, firm reasoning and brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: He ought to propound his advise, in such forme of speech, as may make the truth most evidently appear; that is to say, with as firme ratiocination, as significant and proper language, and as briefly, as the evidence will permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good counsel uses rigorous argumentation, precise language, and concision; avoid rash, unevident inferences, obscure or ambiguous expressions, metaphors stirring passion, or other rhetorical devices used to persuade rather than to prove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence requirement: experience and study
rubrics_metrics.description: No Man Is Presumed To Be A Good Counsellour, But In Such Businesse, As He Hath Not Onely Been Much Versed In, But Hath Also Much Meditated On, And Considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel quality depends on domain-specific experience and reflection; one is only a reliable adviser in matters one has practised and studied; when infallible rules exist (e.g., geometry/engineering), rule-followers may outrank general experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign affairs require specialized intelligence and records
rubrics_metrics.description: To be able to give Counsell to a Common-wealth, in a businesse that hath reference to another Common-wealth, It Is Necessary To Be Acquainted With The Intelligences, And Letters That Come From Thence, And With All The Records Of Treaties, And Other Transactions Of State Between Them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisers on foreign policy must have access to dispatches, treaties, and records; without such materials their counsel is likely unsound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer private consultation to large assemblies for counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A man is better Counselled by hearing them apart, then in an Assembly... in hearing every man apart, you have the advice of every man; but in an Assembly... they deliver their advise... moved by the eloquence of another, or for feare of displeasing...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate hearings prevent group conformity, allow testing of reasons via interruption and objections, and reduce the influence of passion-driven eloquence; assemblies can produce heated, secretive, or ambitious interventions that harm deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislator and law: only sovereign makes law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Legislator in all Common-wealths, is only the Soveraign, be he one Man, as in a Monarchy, or one Assembly of men, as in a Democracy, or Aristocracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law is a command of the commonwealth and thus only the sovereign (the representative person) can create or abrogate laws; subordinate judges or private persons cannot legitimately make law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign not subject to civil laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soveraign of a Common-wealth, be it an Assembly, or one Man, is not subject to the Civill Lawes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the sovereign can make and repeal laws at will, he cannot be bound by civil laws in a way that would prevent his acting as legislator; ability to release oneself from laws implies lack of binding self-subjection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom requires sovereign assent to be law
rubrics_metrics.description: When long Use obtaineth the authority of a Law, it is not the Length of Time that maketh the Authority, but the Will of the Soveraign signified by his silence (for Silence is sometimes an argument of Consent); and it is no longer Law, then the Soveraign shall be silent therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescription or long usage only become authoritative law through sovereign approbation (explicit or tacit); historical longevity alone does not override sovereign will or equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrelation of natural law and civil law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law of Nature, and the Civill Law, contain each other, and are of equall extent... The Law of Nature therefore is a part of the Civill Law in all Common-wealths of the world. Reciprocally also, the Civill Law is a part of the Dictates of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural dictates (equity, justice, fidelity) become legally binding within a settled commonwealth; conversely civil obligations (e.g., obedience to covenant) fall under natural law — the two are integrated rather than wholly separate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provincial/customary laws derive force from current sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there be divers Provinces... diversity of Lawes, which commonly are called the Customes of each severall Province, we are not to understand that such Customes have their Force, onely from Length of Time; but that they were antiently Lawes written, or otherwise made known, for the Constitutions, and Statutes of their Soveraigns; and are now Lawes, not by vertue of the Praescription of time, but by the Constitutions of their present Soveraigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local customs persist only insofar as current sovereigns recognize or adopt them; their authority is not inherent in age alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law must be made known and traceable to sovereign authority
rubrics_metrics.description: From this, that the Law is a Command... we may understand, that the Command of the Common-wealth, is Law onely to those, that have means to take notice of it... Nor is it enough the Law be written, and published; but also that there be manifest signs, that it proceedeth from the will of the Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rule is not law for someone unless it has been sufficiently declared to them and shown to emanate from the sovereign; this prevents private actors from falsely publishing fraudulent 'laws' and grounds excusal where notice is impossible (e.g., incompetents, children, insane).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwritten laws binding universally are laws of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: If it be a Law that obliges all the Subjects without exception, and is not written, nor otherwise published... it is a Law of Nature... For whatsoever men are to take knowledge of for Law... must be such as is agreeable to the reason of all men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General, unwritten obligations that everyone can discover by reason (e.g., the Golden Rule) are natural law and do not require proclamation to bind; unwritten obligations limited to particular conditions are likewise derived from natural reason in those conditions (e.g., ministerial fidelity when written instructions absent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on claims that law can never be against reason
rubrics_metrics.description: That Law can never be against Reason, our Lawyers are agreed... the doubt is, of whose Reason it is, that shall be received for Law... it is not that Juris Prudentia... but the Reason of this our Artificiall Man the Common-wealth, and his Command, that maketh Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While law should accord with reason, Hobbes locates that reason in the sovereign's will as representative of the commonwealth; disputes about 'reason' should be resolved by reference to the commonwealth's declared purpose and commands rather than private judges' independent constructions.
